review_scope: Registered-source content review of the published Annals of Statistics 52(2), 2024, pages 729-756, DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2366, by Yuling Yan, Yuxin Chen and Jianqing Fan. All 28 PDF pages belong to the main paper. Discussion, acknowledgments and funding end on page 24; the supplement notice on page 25 is followed by references through page 28. The separate supplement was not opened. Fresh text evidence covers all 28 pages; source passages, formulas and boundary pages were inspected visually.
inventory: Exactly five actual THEOREM headings occur on physical pages 7,9,11,12,21. Theorem 5 continues on page 22. Complete hypotheses, formulas, cases and conclusions were checked. Citations to higher-numbered supplement theorems and other result types are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 1 preserves independent Gaussian columns, the sampling model, p bounded away from one or p=1, all comparability and noise conditions, log^9 and log^7 sample restrictions, and the complete iteration formula. A fresh magnified crop confirms that its first denominator is sqrt(nd) times p. The random rotation, row quantifier, convex-set distance and full population covariance with d_li-star are retained.
Theorem 2 preserves the inherited hypotheses, its sign-based rotation and supremum of marginal rowwise coverage errors. It does not state joint simultaneous coverage of all rows.

Theorem 3 retains the lower bound on the two selected row norms, its own log^7 sampling condition, both noise restrictions, Assumption 1, and the reference to the iteration condition (3.6). The theorem does not import Theorem 1's stronger log^9 sampling condition.
Theorem 4 retains the conditions of Theorem 3 and its added log^8 sampling restriction, with the interval explicitly computed by Algorithm 4.

Theorem 5 preserves Assumptions 2-3, both dimension conditions, the source small-constant meaning of <<, and the starred singular value in the iteration count despite its conflict with natural-marked model notation. Its probability event, decomposition, second-order term and all three residual bounds on page 22 are complete.
source_passages: All 18 source entries and 10 auxiliary passages were reviewed. The Gaussian-column covariance model, independent Bernoulli sampling, row-specific sub-Gaussian noises, zero-filled observations, coordinate/diagonal projections and nonsingular matrix-sign definition match pages 1-4. The signal-extension footnote remains separate from the Gaussian theorem wording.

Population eigenvalue scales and their condition number, Definition 1 incoherence and Assumption 1 noise variance ratio match pages 5-6. Algorithm 2 retains the 1/(np^2) scaling, inclusive loop and t_0 outputs. Algorithm 3 retains the observed-row variance estimates, full covariance estimate and chi-square-ball confidence construction.

Both population covariance-entry variance formulas match page 10; the diagonal case is distinct from substituting equal indices in the off-diagonal case. Algorithm 4 preserves both cases and its printed population S-star_jj term. Its normal quantile differs from Algorithm 3's chi-square construction.

The rectangular model, n=max(n_1,n_2), singular-value condition number, all three Assumption 2 inequalities and complete bounded-noise Assumption 3 match page 20. The printed var(E_ij squared) and square noise-index range remain unaltered. Algorithm 5, the orthogonal minimization and both zeta abbreviations match page 21.
dependency_review: All 35 direct uses and 48 related theorem connections were checked, including every direct list, every local reach set and every reported path. The two model branches share only generic projection primitives. Theorem 5 does not inherit PCA Gaussian columns, sampling, noise ratio or Definition 1. Theorems 1-4 do not inherit the general-model assumptions through proof use of Theorem 5. Algorithm 3 reaches only Theorem 2; Algorithm 4 only Theorem 4. The population entry variance reaches Theorems 3/4; the matrix-sign definition reaches only Theorems 1/2. The general-model rotation uses its own argmin definition.
names_and_highlights: All 18 interfaces use source natural-language keywords, original source types and labels. Adjacent naming contexts and selectors were checked against the definitions, assumptions, algorithms or related same-paper theorem statements. Definition 1 and Assumption 2 remain separate despite sharing the word incoherence. Both HeteroPCA constructions retain their distinct input models and scaling.
source_limitations: The 22 existing source notes were checked. They preserve the population term in Algorithm 4, variance-of-square expression, star/natural mismatch, rectangular indexing mismatch, broad sub-Gaussian footnote, implicit cross-independence, zero noise-ratio convention, singular matrix-sign outcomes, eigenselection and loop conventions, empty rows and negative variance estimates, row/column identification, marginal versus simultaneous coverage, row quantifiers, differing logarithmic sample restrictions, source comparison notation, different condition numbers and dimensions, distinct incoherence and noise assumptions, zero singular values, confidence-level scope, the decomposition event, argmin selection and excluded supplement/proof references. Faithful source extraction does not certify the source's mathematical claims.
changes: No census-content correction was required. The saved per-paper rebuild now resolves the fixed verified local PDF. Earlier scripts are archived, and the original audit and all six extracted JSON artifacts remain unchanged.
validation: Independent inventory and census validators pass. All six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Source identity, full main-paper text, exact heading enumeration, continuation pages, dependency sets, selector occurrence and artifact hashes supplement the completed manual review.
